TITLE: Multi-Task Learning for Diffusion Planners
PROPOSAL: We explore the potential of multi-task learning (MTL) to improve planner generalization and adaptability in the maze navigation, legged robot locomotion, and mobile robot navigation domains. By training a single diffusion planner to perform multiple tasks simultaneously, we aim to capture underlying task-agnostic dynamics and leverage task-related knowledge to enhance transferability and performance.
CONTROLS: We will compare to a baseline that trains separate planners for each domain and ablate the effect of MTL on planner performance.
COST: 28
PREDICTION: We expect the MTL planners to demonstrate improved transferability and performance across domains, particularly for tasks with similar dynamics or requirements. However, we may see performance degradation if the MTL strategy fails to capture task-specific knowledge or overlooks task-related variability.

TITLE: Non-Deterministic Deep Brain Encoding Model
PROPOSAL: Modify the existing MindSimulator model by adding a non-deterministic decoder, replacing the deterministic MLP-based autoencoder, with a stochastic VAE (Variational Autoencoder). The VAE will generate a Gaussian distribution of fMRI patterns conditioned on semantic features, introducing variability in neural responses at the synthesis stage. The diffusion-based semantic-to-latent mapping module remains intact to align the fMRI latent space with visual stimuli.
CONTROLS: Compare the modified model to the baseline deterministic MindSimulator model and evaluate its recovery of voxel-wise variability using metrics such as voxel-wise correlation coefficient.
COST: 30
PREDICTION: The modified model is expected to capture the one-to-many nature of brain activity, encoding visual stimuli consistently in a probabilistic manner. However, it may face challenges in aligning the probabilistic fMRI patterns with the deterministic visual stimuli, leading to variability in the semantic consistency of the output.

TITLE: Alignment-based Sequence Sorting for Efficient Bidirectional Learning
PROPOSAL: Given the long-range dependencies commonly observed in amino acid sequences, we propose an instantiation of sequence sorting to expedite bidirectional learning. Our technique arranges input sequences in an alternating order such that proximal elements are aligned, reducing the effect of sequence length on the temporal complexity of bidirectional processing. Furthermore, to improve the versatility and adaptability of the sorting approach, we develop a neural network-based sequence watermarking scheme to selectively emphasize specific sequence features (e.g. signal peptide, domain boundaries) during the sorting process, enabling more informed sequence alignments and knowledge distillation.
CONTROLS: We compare our alignment-based sequence sorting and watermarking framework against standard sequence processing methods on synthetically-lengthened datasets to demonstrate its performance under differing levels of sequence complexity and various feature emphases.
COST: 700 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Expected to observe improved bidirectional learning performance, adaptability, and knowledge distillation properties, with potential applications in protein structure prediction and design, where precise control over sequence features is crucial.

ACTION: REVISE 3
TITLE: Hybrid Query-Driven and Temporally-Informed Frame Selection for Efficient Video Question Answering
PROPOSAL: To further improve the performance of our hybrid query-driven and temporally-informed frame selection approach, we propose to incorporate a reinforcement learning module that adapts the frame selection policy based on the rewards received from the question answering model.
